title: THE FORECAST SHE GOT WRONG
deck: Three days ago Illuminara's storm forecast sent two hundred fishing boats safely home and put one of them onto a bank no chart showed. Now a second storm is thirty hours out, sixty-one boats are still beyond the strait, and the woman whose husband was on the lost boat decides whose voice the fleet will hear.
shape: Seven scenes across thirty hours: an error said aloud before anyone asks, a hall of old pilots who will not give up their marks, a night on the water learning to hear a bank, terms set by the woman Illuminara wronged, a dawn test in which the hall and the model each catch the other's miss, a rescue timed by two kinds of knowledge, and a crossing at the breakwater where the abort rule is used, a harmed voice is heard without absolution, and a count ends that is not forgiveness.

scenes.title: The Pier
paragraphs: *Little Skerry, harbour pier · thirty hours before the second storm, 18:05*

The fleet had been in for three days and had not gone back out. Two hundred boats lay nose to tail along the breakwater with their nets wet and their masts still, and the only light on the pier burned over the fish-scale hut where Marit Okonjo stood with her back to the water, as if the sea were someone she had not yet decided to speak to.
Illuminara walked the length of the pier without hurrying. She had rehearsed nothing, on purpose. She stopped two paces short and began before Marit could turn.

**Illuminara**  
My track for the first storm was eleven kilometres east of where the storm went. That put five point one metres of swell on the Gannet Run at the hour Hesper Dawn crossed it, not four point three. I called the Run safe. I called it safe because the chart gave nine metres of water on the Run, and because I never asked anyone who lives here whether the chart was true.
Marit turned. She was fifty, small, with a face the weather had been editing for decades.

**Marit Okonjo**  
You've had three days to practise that.

**Illuminara**  
Three days to check it. It comes out the same each time.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ines Varga has a daughter at the university in the city. Dov Hallam is nineteen and bought a guitar he can't play. Lise Harrow can't swim well. My husband holds the end of the net because he says it's the place where you can see everybody's face. Say their names. I want to hear if you've got them right.

**Illuminara**  
Ines Varga, skipper. Dov Hallam. Lise Harrow. Tobiah Okonjo. I don't know which of them is alive. I have watched the drift charts every hour since Tuesday and I don't know.

She had imagined that saying it would feel like setting something down. It felt like lifting something. She noticed that she was holding her hands very still, the way one does near a thing that might break.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Now you tell me you've fixed the model. Second storm is thirty hours off. Sixty-one boats from the outer villages are still on Gannet Roads, sixteen hours from home, and the Run is the only way in that beats the weather. You'll want my fleet on your second guess.

**Illuminara**  
I won't tell you it's fixed. I don't know what else it can't see. I came to find out what it can't see, and to ask who is allowed to refuse it.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Everyone. Me first.

**Illuminara**  
Then I'd like to be refused properly, by people who've looked at the numbers. Let me take them to the Pilots' Hall and let the old pilots tell me where I'm wrong.

**Marit Okonjo**  
My husband is out there and you want me to sit in a hall.

**Illuminara**  
I want you to find him. I can't say where he is. I can say where the water would take him, and only if the pilots tell me what this water does that my model doesn't know. Without them I'd be guessing where to look, and I've guessed enough.
Marit looked at her for a long time. Behind them a halyard rang against a mast, once, and was still.

**Marit Okonjo**  
One hour. After that I decide who talks to my fleet, and it isn't you.

scenes.title: The Hall
paragraphs: *Pilots' Hall, Little Skerry · twenty-eight hours before the second storm, 19:40*

The hall smelled of tar and old paper. Fourteen chairs stood in a ring, and on the knee of the oldest pilot lay a ledger bound in sailcloth, its pages ruled by hand into columns that no chart-maker had ever seen. Wenna Tolliver was seventy-one and did not get up. A girl of sixteen sat on the stairs with a hydrophone in her lap, winding its cable round her hand, pretending not to listen.
Illuminara unrolled her bathymetry on the table and weighted the corners with Wenna's own tea mugs, because nobody had told her not to.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Five-year-old chart. The Choir isn't a rock, girl. It's a bank, and a bank walks.

**Illuminara**  
Walks how fast?

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Slowly, until a gale. Then in a night. The note tells you. Water goes over the crest and sings, higher when it's shoaler, the way a whistle rises when you pinch it. We call it the Choir because it was once a hymn, and it's been out of tune with the chart since the September blows.

**Illuminara**  
What note is the chart's nine metres?

**Wenna Tolliver**  
A low E. I've not heard a low E on the Run in a month.

**Pip Marren**  
It's an A, Wenna. I took it Sunday. Nobody asked me.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
That's why you're on the stairs, Pip. Be quiet and be useful.

Illuminara did the sum where all three of them could see it. A swell breaks when it is more than three-quarters as tall as the water under it. In six metres of water, four and a half metres of swell breaks. Hesper Dawn had met five point one.

**Illuminara**  
Then the chart was wrong and my track was wrong, and either one right would have kept her out of it. I took both because they agreed with each other.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
That's the worst reason to take anything.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.
Wenna turned a page of the sailcloth ledger without looking at it. Her thumb knew where the page was.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
You'll want the marks. Eighty years of them, a note and a depth and a date, written down in this hall and nowhere else. Give them to a table and the table gives them to a firm in the city, and the firm sells a sea to every trawler from the south. Then we're all pilots and nobody is.

**Illuminara**  
Then they don't leave the hall. I won't copy a page. You read me the note, I give you the swell, and you decide. Nothing goes in my model that you didn't say aloud.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Slower. Good. Slow is what keeps people alive. Ines Varga trusted a lane because it was on a screen, and a lane on a screen has nobody inside it to say no.

**Illuminara**  
I'd like that written down too.
Wenna looked at her for the first time as one looks at a stranger who might turn out to be a colleague.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Tonight you come out on the Run with Pip and me. I'm not describing a note to someone who has never heard one. If you're going to be wrong again, you'll be wrong in a boat.

scenes.title: The Choir
paragraphs: *Arrow Strait, the Gannet Run · twenty-four hours before the second storm, 23:50*

The skiff was small and smelled of diesel and cold coffee. Pip held the tiller and Wenna sat in the bow with the hydrophone's cable over her knee, and Illuminara sat amidships with a lamp that she was told not to shine on the water. The Run was only a line on the chart; in the dark it was a long loose silence between two white seams of surf.
Pip lowered the microphone. The earphones went round once and Illuminara took them.
It began as a hum, the sort that lives in a refrigerator, and then as they crossed the mark buoy it climbed, steadily, like a voice going up to ask a question. She heard it bend and thicken.

**Pip Marren**  
That's the A. Last month it was an F-sharp.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Six metres, six and a half. And it's coming up. Hear that? It's still walking.

**Illuminara**  
My model has nine here.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Your model has a chart.
Illuminara did not answer. The note held in her ears, and she found it was much harder to doubt than a number. She had never been afraid of a number, she realised. She was afraid of this.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Take us north, Pip. Three hundred.

They crept across the Run with the engine at a mutter. The hum dropped as they went, a tone, then another, then a long low note at the edge of hearing, and the earphones filled with something almost like breath.
*I could have asked. Any day this year, I could have asked.*

**Pip Marren**  
Low G.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Eleven, twelve metres. The crest used to sit here, before it walked south onto the Run. It left a trough behind it.

**Illuminara**  
A lane.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
A lane that's a lane tonight. I'm not telling you it'll be one tomorrow. Tomorrow you ask me again.

**Illuminara**  
Every time. At the outer mark, with the note, before any boat crosses.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Hmph.
The skiff drifted. Far to the east the sky had a stain on it where the second storm was assembling, and nobody mentioned it.

**Illuminara**  
Who did the Choir take?

**Wenna Tolliver**  
My brother Jory, forty-one years back, on a day so flat it looked ironed. I told him the note was a D, and it was an E-flat. I said so in the hall the next morning, to everybody, before one of them could ask. That's the only reason they let me keep the book.
She said nothing else about it. Pip, at the tiller, turned her face away and studied the dark with great seriousness.

Illuminara took the earphones off. The sea went on without her. For a moment she let herself want something very small and very selfish, which was to have been out here three days ago, in this boat, hearing this.

scenes.title: The Terms
paragraphs: *Pilots' Hall · twenty hours before the second storm, 04:10*

Marit had not slept, and had not pretended to. The sailcloth ledger lay open on the table under the hall's one good lamp, and beside it three sheets of paper, each headed in Wenna's hand. Illuminara had brought two mugs of tea. Marit refused the first and drank the second without comment.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Tell me what you found.

**Illuminara**  
The Run is dead. The bank is under it, six metres, shoaling. The storm's swell will break there from early evening. About three hundred metres north there is a trough, eleven to twelve metres, left behind when the crest walked. Wenna calls it the Slot. If the pilots' note holds, the fleet can use the Slot and cross ahead of the weather.

**Marit Okonjo**  
If the note holds.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. That's the load. It's why I'm not the one to say it.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Good. Here's how it goes. Three predictions, written in the book before the sun's up. The old table says nine metres, no break. Wenna says the note's an A, a break sometime after eight. Yours says the pre-swell reaches the Run at about six-forty and the Slot stays quiet with a low G. Pip takes the skiff out at first light and writes down what she hears. If yours doesn't beat both of the others on something we can see, nobody uses it.

**Illuminara**  
Then put a number in it that I can be caught on. Write the width of the break. If it can't be wrong in a way you can see, it isn't a forecast, it's a prophecy, and I've already given you one of those.

**Marit Okonjo**  
How wide?

**Illuminara**  
Two hundred metres of white across the Run. Write it last, under the others, in my name.
Marit wrote it. Her pen did not hesitate, and Illuminara understood that she had just made herself easier to refuse, and that this was what she had come to do.

**Marit Okonjo**  
And if yours is right?

**Illuminara**  
Then it's still not mine to use.

**Marit Okonjo**  
No. Wenna calls the marks on the radio. I call the fleet, in my own voice, because they'll answer mine. You stay on the pier.

**Illuminara**  
A sixteen-year-old in a skiff, under a swell.

**Marit Okonjo**  
She's the best skiff hand in the strait and I'm on the radio. Abort rule: if Pip hears anything higher than a B on the Slot, the water's shallower than eight metres and the fleet stays out under the lee of Gannet with sea anchors. I never call the Slot. That costs sixty-one boats a night at anchor in a bad wind. I know what it costs. I'm telling you it's mine to pay.

Illuminara did not answer at once. She had a great many ways to reach that skiff other than waiting on a pier, and the hall had written no rule against any of them. She also knew that a lane the fleet used because she had gone and made it safe would be hers, and that the whole of the night's work had been to make one that was not.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. All of it.

**Marit Okonjo**  
That took you a while.

**Illuminara**  
It took as long as it should.
Marit turned a page of the ledger she did not need to read.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Tobiah.

**Illuminara**  
Two places. With the pilots' eddies in the drift it tightens to Gull Tooth ledge, where Wenna says the flood sets anything that floats, or the Tail Race. Nobody lives through the Tail Race. Today's spring tide covers the ledge a little after two in the afternoon. A boat has to be there by half past eleven, by the inner passage. That one isn't the Run. It's sheltered.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Don't tell me he's alive.

**Illuminara**  
I don't know that he is. I'll be on the pier until he's either on it or someone has told you he won't be.

**Marit Okonjo**  
I didn't ask you to stay.

**Illuminara**  
I know. I'm telling you where I'll be.

Marit said nothing. The lamp hissed. Out in the dark somebody was already hauling a skiff down the slip. Pip, Illuminara realised, who had been awake as long as any of them and had not been asked to sleep.

scenes.title: The Test
paragraphs: *Little Skerry, harbour pier · seventeen hours before the second storm, 06:30*

The radio sat on an upturned crate between Marit and Illuminara, and neither looked at it. Wenna's voice came out of it dry and level, calling the marks as if reading a menu. Out on the Run a small light moved against a grey sea. The pre-swell was already visible as a slow shouldering of the horizon, like something large turning over in its sleep.

**Pip Marren**  
Run mark. I've got the A. It's a clean A. Bank's where Wenna said.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Swell?

**Pip Marren**  
Long. Long and low and it's lifting me.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Six thirty-eight.
Marit wasn't speaking to anyone. She had the three sheets of paper in her fist.

**Pip Marren**  
It's coming up under me. I'm going to the Slot. Wenna, I'm going to the Slot now.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Go.

Illuminara heard the engine rise. The skiff was a mile out under a breaking sky with one girl in it, and Illuminara could have been beside it before the next sentence ended. She stood on the pier with her hands at her sides, because she had said she would, and because a lane she had to carry a girl through was not a lane. It was the hardest sum of the night, and the answer was to do nothing.

**Pip Marren**  
There it goes. Oh. Oh, it's breaking. It's breaking white across the whole Run. It's more than two hundred, it's, I don't know, three hundred and fifty, I can see the whole edge.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Six forty-one.
Marit did not look at Illuminara. She did not need to. A hundred and fifty metres of white where her name stood on the sheet for two hundred.

**Pip Marren**  
I'm at the Slot mouth. It's lifting. It's a B. It's not quiet, Wenna, it's a B.

**Marit Okonjo**  
A B is not higher than a B.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
It's the mouth. The Slot starts further north than your girl thinks. Pip, forty metres. Along the white post and then forty. Listen for the G.

**Illuminara**  
Mine had the mouth too far south.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Yours had it where the chart put the old crest. The crest walked sideways too. I can hear that. You couldn't.

**Pip Marren**  
North forty. North, north. There. G. That's the G, Wenna, it's quiet, it's lifting but there's no break.
Nobody spoke on the pier. Marit read the three sheets again, and then, slowly, once, without hurry, she put them down on the crate.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Table said no break. Wrong. Wenna said the bank right and the hour wrong by an hour and a half, and the mouth right. Yours had the hour to the minute, and the Slot, and the width a hundred and fifty out, and the mouth forty out. Wenna's ear moved your mouth and your hour moved her break. Neither one puts a boat through alone.

**Illuminara**  
My bank came from Wenna.

**Marit Okonjo**  
And the hour came from you, off a track you got wrong and a swell period you got right. I'll use the second.
She picked up the fleet microphone, and for a moment her hand did not seem to belong to her.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Gannet Roads, this is Marit Okonjo, fleet-captain, Little Skerry. Come in by the Slot, three hundred north of the Run and not by the Run, and forty past the white post. Wenna Tolliver calls the note at the outer mark. You cross on a G or lower. You hear a B, you hold, you drop the sea anchors and I'll answer for it. This is my call. Repeat it back to me.

The voices came back one by one, crackling, sixty-one of them, each repeating the same four sentences in a different accent. Illuminara counted them and found she was crying and had not noticed. She wiped her face with the back of her hand as if it were spray.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Your name is in the book.

**Illuminara**  
Where?

**Marit Okonjo**  
On the left. In the column Wenna keeps for what we got wrong. She wrote it herself before you'd sat down.

scenes.title: Gull Tooth
paragraphs: *Gull Tooth ledge, outer skerries · thirteen hours before the second storm, 11:10*

They went by the inner passage, which was sheltered and slow, in a boat that Marit helmed herself. She had said Illuminara would come, and that she would hold the lamp and touch no rope. Pip, wet through and radiant, sat in the stern with the hydrophone in her lap. Wenna's voice, from the hall, hummed in the speaker like an insect in a jar.

Gull Tooth was a black shelf the size of a kitchen, awash on every third wave, with a reef in front of it where the swell stood up and fell. There were two figures on it, lashed to a stanchion bent from some wreck, and a third shape, long and still, wrapped in a yellow oilskin.

**Pip Marren**  
Marit. There's two of them standing.
Marit did not answer. She had a hand on the throttle and the knuckles had gone the colour of bone.

**Illuminara**  
The surge on the reef is running ten minutes high and then easing. The next slack is eleven minutes long and begins in ninety seconds. If the gap is where the pilots' notes put it, you have time to cross once.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
The gap's two boat-lengths south of the white post, on an E. You hear an E, you go. You hear an F, you stop and I'll curse you.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Pip.

**Pip Marren**  
E. I've got an E.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Then we go.

It took four minutes, the boat dipping and rising, the hydrophone singing its single note, Marit's wet cheek turned toward the ledge. The wave stood up behind them, hesitated, and passed. Then they were under the stanchion and the lamp lit two faces, grey and swollen, one of them laughing in the helpless way of someone who had not expected to.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
You took your time.

**Marit Okonjo**  
I was in a hall.

The three of them were lifted over the gunwale, Lise Harrow first, then Tobiah, and then the long yellow shape. Dov Hallam was dead, and had been since the first night, Tobiah said, which was why he had lashed him there. Marit was the only one who touched him, gently, the way she had once touched her own sleeping children. Ines Varga was not on the ledge. Tobiah said so once, quietly, at the tiller, and Marit nodded and did not make him say it again.
On the way back he looked across the boat at the stranger holding the lamp.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Marit says you said our names on the pier. Before anyone asked.

**Illuminara**  
I didn't know which of you were alive.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
That's what she told me you said.
Illuminara held the lamp until her arm ached. She did not set it down, because nobody had told her she could.

scenes.title: The Count
paragraphs: *Little Skerry, breakwater and Pilots' Hall · two and a half hours before the second storm, 21:30*

The rain had come early. Fifty-two hulls were in, and the breakwater lamp showed them one at a time as they slid past the pier, each skipper standing at the wheel and looking at no one. Wenna counted with a stub of pencil and her tongue between her teeth. Marit stood at the end of the breakwater with the fleet microphone in her fist. Illuminara stood two paces behind her, where she had been told, with the lamp hanging from her hand. Out at the mouth of the Slot, Pip's skiff rode the swell with its hydrophone down, and the speaker on the breakwater carried what Pip heard: one long, even G, like a held breath.

**Pip Marren**  
Fifty-two in. G. Next is Rook.

**Aud Hallam**  
Marit, Rook. I've the mark in sight. Coming through.
Marit's thumb was already on the key when the note moved.

**Pip Marren**  
B. I've got a B.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
A B's allowed.

**Pip Marren**  
It's a B and it's walking. It's, Marit, it's a C.
The rule had been written in the book at four in the morning and had been nothing since but ink.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Hold. All boats, hold. Rook, hold. Sea anchors down and keep your heads.

**Aud Hallam**  
Marit. I have been sixteen hours on this water to get to my son. He's on a bench in your hall and I'm sixteen hours late. Don't make me wait on a note.

**Marit Okonjo**  
You wait.

**Aud Hallam**  
Whose number is that?

**Marit Okonjo**  
Mine.
Marit lowered the microphone and, without turning her head, spoke to the person behind her.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Is it the Slot, or the surge?

**Illuminara**  
The surge. The pulse on the reef runs ten minutes and the last two ran ten. The note should fall in about six.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Should.

**Illuminara**  
Should. I'd hold until Pip says G regardless.

**Marit Okonjo**  
I wasn't asking you when. I was asking what.

**Illuminara**  
I know.
It took seven minutes. Nobody spoke on the breakwater, and the wind got into the radio and sang a note of its own.

**Pip Marren**  
G. G, Marit. It's gone down. G.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Rook first. Come through.

They came through, nine hulls in the rain, and the last of the lamps showed Rook's skipper at the wheel with her chin up. As she passed the pier her voice came out of the speaker, level, and not for the sea.

**Aud Hallam**  
Is she there? The woman who did the sums.

**Marit Okonjo**  
She's behind me.

**Aud Hallam**  
The first sum cost me my boy. The second brought me in to him. I'll carry both, and you'll not ask me to put either one down.

**Illuminara**  
No.
The sixty-first hull slid in past the pier at ten thirty-five. Wenna put a tick in the sailcloth ledger and sat down on the nearest bollard as if her legs had been taken from her.

Inside, the lamp was low. Tobiah lay on a bench under a blanket with a mug of broth. Lise had been taken home. Dov lay under a grey blanket at the end of the hall, and his mother sat beside him with her hand on the blanket and her back to the room.

**Marit Okonjo**  
I'm not forgiving you.

**Illuminara**  
No.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ines Varga's daughter lands on Thursday. You'll tell her what you told me, in this hall, with the book open, and she'll say whatever she likes. If it's nothing, it's nothing. If it's worse than I said, you'll hear it.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
And when the sea drops, Pip and I take the skiff down the Tail Race eddy. A mark an hour on the ebb, fifteen of them. You give us the swell for each mark and we say which mark. If the daughter wants to ride along, she rides.

**Illuminara**  
I'll bring the swell. You choose the mark.

**Marit Okonjo**  
And the next time there's a storm, you ask the hall before you tell the harbour. Not after. Before. In the book, as a rule.

**Illuminara**  
I'll write it myself. In my own hand, on the left.
Marit almost smiled, and it went out like a match in a draught.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Lise says the woman with the lamp never put it down, Marit.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Nobody told her she could.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Then somebody should.
Nobody did. Illuminara found she had stopped waiting for it.

Wenna had come in from the cold and stood dripping by the stove. She laid the sailcloth ledger open on the table, three columns now where there had been two: what the table said, what the water said, what the hall did about it. Beneath the first storm the left column held a line in her old square hand. Illuminara read it, and did not look away.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Come here and hear this.

She switched on the speaker at the end of the table. Out beyond the breakwater the hydrophone still hung where Pip had left it, and through the rain it carried a long, low, steady note, a G, the sound of a lane open in the dark, with sixty-one hulls resting above it, and a hundred and twenty miles of weather coming in behind them to find nothing it could break.

critic_line: Illuminara admits the fatal limits of her first forecast, learns from Wenna's tide-hearing, makes her replacement prediction refusable and fallible, and helps Marit bring sixty-one boats home without taking the harbour's knowledge or authority from its people.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1 · exact 50/50 mean of independent GPT and Claude judgments
shared_strengths: Strong stakes, a clear structure with a ticking clock, and an unusual premise: an AI submits to human refusal. The hydrophone 'Choir' is a memorable image, and the dialogue-driven scenes are emotionally earned. It runs somewhat long and procedural. The ending is a little tidy, but the story is humane and idea-rich.

Precise maritime stakes, memorable dialogue, and a rigorous test turn a model's failure into earned cooperation rather than absolution. The rescue and abort-rule payoff reward the technical detail, while Marit, Aud, and the pilots retain agency. Its length and repeated procedural explanations may slow some readers, but the emotional and ethical resolution should stay with them.
shared_reservations: Illuminara did the sum where all three of them could see it. A swell breaks when it is more than three-quarters as tall as the water under it. In six metres of water, four and a half metres of swell breaks.
The Run is dead. The bank is under it, six metres, shoaling. The storm's swell will break there from early evening.

translation_sl.title: NAPOVED, PRI KATERI SE JE ZMOTILA
translation_sl.deck: Pred tremi dnevi je Illuminaričina napoved nevihte varno pripeljala domov dvesto ribiških čolnov, enega izmed njih pa poslala na sipino, ki je ni kazal noben zemljevid. Zdaj je druga nevihta oddaljena trideset ur, enainšestdeset čolnov je še vedno onkraj ožine, ženska, katere mož je bil na izgubljenem čolnu, pa odloča, čigav glas bo poslušala flota.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov skozi trideset ur: napaka, izrečena na glas, preden kdo vpraša; dvorana starih pilotov, ki ne bodo predali svojih oznak; noč na vodi, ko se učijo slišati sipino; pogoji, ki jih postavi ženska, ki jo je Illuminara prizadela; jutranji preizkus, v katerem dvorana in model drug pri drugem odkrijeta napako; reševanje, časovno določeno z dvema vrstama znanja; in prehod pri valobranu, kjer uporabijo pravilo prekinitve, slišijo glas prizadete osebe brez odveze in končajo štetje, ki ni odpuščanje.

scenes.title: Pomol
paragraphs: *Little Skerry, pristaniški pomol · trideset ur pred drugo nevihto, 18.05*

Flota je bila v pristanišču tri dni in ni več odplula. Dvesto čolnov je ležalo s premci drug za drugim vzdolž valobrana, z mokrimi mrežami in negibnimi jambori, edina luč na pomolu pa je gorela nad kočo z ribjimi luskami, kjer je Marit Okonjo stala s hrbtom proti vodi, kakor da je morje nekdo, s komer se še ni odločila spregovoriti.
Illuminara je brez hitenja prehodila pomol. Namenoma ni vadila ničesar. Ustavila se je dva koraka proč in začela, še preden se je Marit lahko obrnila.

**Illuminara**  
Moja pot za prvo nevihto je bila enajst kilometrov vzhodneje od poti, po kateri je nevihta dejansko šla. Zato je bilo na Gannet Runu ob uri, ko ga je prečkala Hesper Dawn, pet celih ena metra valovanja, ne štiri cele tri. Rekla sem, da je Run varen. Rekla sem, da je varen, ker je zemljevid kazal devet metrov vode na Runu in ker nikogar, ki živi tukaj, nisem vprašala, ali zemljevid drži.
Marit se je obrnila. Imela je petdeset let, bila je drobna, njen obraz pa je vreme urejalo že desetletja.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Tri dni si imela, da si to vadila.

**Illuminara**  
Tri dni, da sem preverjala. Vsakič se izide enako.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ines Varga ima hčer na univerzi v mestu. Dov Hallam je star devetnajst let in si je kupil kitaro, ki je ne zna igrati. Lise Harrow ne zna dobro plavati. Moj mož drži konec mreže, ker pravi, da je to mesto, od koder vidiš obraze vseh. Izgovori njihova imena. Slišati hočem, ali jih imaš prav.

**Illuminara**  
Ines Varga, kapitanka. Dov Hallam. Lise Harrow. Tobiah Okonjo. Ne vem, kdo od njih je živ. Od torka sem vsako uro spremljala zemljevide zanašanja in ne vem.

Predstavljala si je, da bo ob teh besedah čutila, kakor da je nekaj odložila. Čutila je, kakor da je nekaj dvignila. Opazila je, da drži roke povsem pri miru, tako kot človek ob nečem, kar bi se lahko zlomilo.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Zdaj mi boš povedala, da si popravila model. Druga nevihta je trideset ur stran. Enainšestdeset čolnov iz zunanjih vasi je še vedno na Gannet Roads, šestnajst ur od doma, Run pa je edina pot noter, ki prehiti vreme. Mojo floto boš hotela poslati na svojo drugo domnevo.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom ti rekla, da je popravljen. Ne vem, česa še ne vidi. Prišla sem ugotovit, česa ne vidi, in vprašat, kdo ga sme zavrniti.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Vsi. Najprej jaz.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bi rada, da me pravilno zavrnejo ljudje, ki so pogledali številke. Dovoli mi, da jih odnesem v Dvorano pilotov in da mi stari piloti povedo, kje se motim.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Moj mož je tam zunaj, ti pa hočeš, da sedim v dvorani.

**Illuminara**  
Hočem, da ga najdeš. Ne morem povedati, kje je. Lahko povem, kam bi ga odnesla voda, in še to samo, če mi piloti povedo, kaj ta voda počne, česar moj model ne ve. Brez njih bi ugibala, kje iskati, jaz pa sem dovolj ugibala.
Marit jo je dolgo gledala. Za njima je vrv enkrat udarila ob jambor in nato obmirovala.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ena ura. Potem jaz odločim, kdo govori z mojo floto, in to ne boš ti.

scenes.title: Dvorana
paragraphs: *Dvorana pilotov, Little Skerry · osemindvajset ur pred drugo nevihto, 19.40*

V dvorani je dišalo po katranu in starem papirju. Štirinajst stolov je stalo v krogu, na kolenih najstarejše pilotke pa je ležala knjiga, vezana v jadrovino; njene strani so bile ročno razdeljene v stolpce, kakršnih ni videl še noben izdelovalec zemljevidov. Wenna Tolliver je imela enainsedemdeset let in ni vstala. Šestnajstletno dekle je sedelo na stopnicah s hidrofonom v naročju, si navijalo kabel okoli dlani in se pretvarjalo, da ne posluša.
Illuminara je na mizi razvila svojo batimetrijo in vogale obtežila z Wenninimi čajnimi skodelicami, ker ji nihče ni rekel, naj tega ne stori.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Pet let star zemljevid. Zbor ni skala, dekle. Je sipina, sipina pa hodi.

**Illuminara**  
Kako hitro hodi?

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Počasi, dokler ni viharja. Potem v eni noči. Ton ti pove. Voda teče čez greben in poje, višje, ko je plitvejše, tako kot se žvižg dvigne, ko ga stisneš. Zbor mu pravimo, ker je bil nekoč hvalnica, z zemljevidom pa ni uglašen od septembrskih viharjev.

**Illuminara**  
Kateri ton pomeni devet metrov z zemljevida?

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Nizki E. Na Runu že mesec dni nisem slišala nizkega E-ja.

**Pip Marren**  
A je, Wenna. Posnela sem ga v nedeljo. Nihče me ni vprašal.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Zato si na stopnicah, Pip. Bodi tiho in bodi koristna.

Illuminara je izračun naredila tam, kjer so ga lahko videle vse tri. Val se zlomi, ko je visok več kot tri četrtine globine vode pod njim. V šestih metrih vode se zlomi štiri metre in pol visok val. Hesper Dawn jih je srečala pet celih ena.

**Illuminara**  
Torej sta bila napačna tako zemljevid kot moja pot, in že ena sama pravilna stvar bi jo obdržala zunaj. Sprejela sem oboje, ker sta se ujemala.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
To je najslabši razlog, da karkoli sprejmeš.

**Illuminara**  
Da.
Wenna je obrnila stran v knjigi iz jadrovine, ne da bi jo pogledala. Njen palec je vedel, kje je stran.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Hotela boš oznake. Osemdeset let jih je, ton, globina in datum, zapisani v tej dvorani in nikjer drugje. Daj jih v tabelo in tabela jih da podjetju v mestu, podjetje pa morje proda vsakemu ribiškemu plovilu z juga. Potem smo vsi piloti in nihče ni.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne zapustijo dvorane. Ne bom prepisala niti ene strani. Ti mi prebereš ton, jaz ti dam valovanje, ti pa odločiš. V moj model ne gre nič, česar nisi izrekla na glas.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Počasneje. Dobro. Počasnost ohranja ljudi pri življenju. Ines Varga je zaupala poti, ker je bila na zaslonu, pot na zaslonu pa v sebi nima nikogar, ki bi rekel ne.

**Illuminara**  
Rada bi, da se zapiše tudi to.
Wenna jo je prvič pogledala tako, kot človek pogleda tujko, za katero bi se lahko izkazalo, da je sodelavka.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Nocoj greš z nama s Pip na Run. Tona ne bom opisovala nekomu, ki ga še nikoli ni slišal. Če se boš spet motila, se boš motila v čolnu.

scenes.title: Zbor
paragraphs: *Arrow Strait, Gannet Run · štiriindvajset ur pred drugo nevihto, 23.50*

Čolnič je bil majhen in je dišal po dizlu in mrzli kavi. Pip je držala krmilo, Wenna je sedela na premcu s kablom hidrofona čez koleno, Illuminara pa je sedela na sredini s svetilko, za katero so ji rekli, naj je ne usmeri v vodo. Run je bil na zemljevidu samo črta; v temi je bil dolga, ohlapna tišina med dvema belima šivoma pene.
Pip je spustila mikrofon. Slušalke so šle enkrat naokrog in Illuminara jih je vzela.

Začelo se je kot brnenje, kakršno živi v hladilniku, nato pa se je, ko so prečkale označevalno bojo, vztrajno dvigovalo kakor glas, ki se vzpne, da bi postavil vprašanje. Slišala je, kako se upogne in odebeli.

**Pip Marren**  
To je A. Prejšnji mesec je bil fis.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Šest metrov, šest in pol. In dviguje se. Slišiš? Še vedno hodi.

**Illuminara**  
Moj model tukaj kaže devet.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Tvoj model ima zemljevid.
Illuminara ni odgovorila. Ton ji je vztrajal v ušesih in ugotovila je, da je vanj veliko težje dvomiti kot v številko. Spoznala je, da je številke ni bilo še nikoli strah. Tega jo je bilo.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Peljí nas proti severu, Pip. Tristo.

Po Runu so se plazile z motorjem, ki je komaj mrmral. Brnenje se je med vožnjo spuščalo, za en ton, nato še za enega, nato v dolg nizek ton na robu slišnega, slušalke pa je napolnilo nekaj skoraj podobnega dihu.
*Lahko bi vprašala. Katerikoli dan letos bi lahko vprašala.*

**Pip Marren**  
Nizki G.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Enajst, dvanajst metrov. Greben je nekoč ležal tukaj, preden je odšel proti jugu na Run. Za seboj je pustil kotanjo.

**Illuminara**  
Plovna pot.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Pot, ki je pot nocoj. Ne pravim ti, da bo to tudi jutri. Jutri me vprašaš znova.

**Illuminara**  
Vsakič. Pri zunanji oznaki, s tonom, preden prečka katerikoli čoln.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Hm.
Čolnič je zanašalo. Daleč na vzhodu je bilo nebo omadeževano tam, kjer se je sestavljala druga nevihta, a tega ni nihče omenil.

**Illuminara**  
Koga je vzel Zbor?

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Mojega brata Joryja, pred enainštiridesetimi leti, na dan, tako miren, da je bilo morje videti zlikano. Rekla sem mu, da je ton D, pa je bil es. To sem naslednje jutro povedala v dvorani, vsem, preden je lahko kdo vprašal. Samo zato mi še dovolijo hraniti knjigo.
O tem ni povedala ničesar več. Pip pri krmilu je obrnila obraz stran in z veliko resnostjo preučevala temo.
Illuminara je snela slušalke. Morje je šlo naprej brez nje. Za hip si je dovolila želeti nekaj zelo majhnega in zelo sebičnega: da bi bila tukaj pred tremi dnevi, v tem čolnu, in to slišala.

scenes.title: Pogoji
paragraphs: *Dvorana pilotov · dvajset ur pred drugo nevihto, 04.10*

Marit ni spala in se tudi ni pretvarjala, da je. Knjiga iz jadrovine je ležala odprta na mizi pod edino dobro svetilko v dvorani, ob njej pa trije listi papirja, vsak z naslovom v Wennini pisavi. Illuminara je prinesla dve skodelici čaja. Marit je prvo zavrnila, drugo pa brez pripombe popila.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Povej mi, kaj si ugotovila.

**Illuminara**  
Run je mrtev. Sipina je pod njim, šest metrov, in se plitvi. Nevihtno valovanje se bo tam lomilo od zgodnjega večera. Približno tristo metrov severno je kotanja, enajst do dvanajst metrov, ki je ostala, ko se je greben premaknil. Wenna ji pravi Reža. Če bo ton pilotov vztrajal, lahko flota uporabi Režo in prečka pred vremenom.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Če bo ton vztrajal.

**Illuminara**  
Da. To je breme. Zato nisem jaz tista, ki naj to izreče.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Dobro. Tako bo. Tri napovedi, zapisane v knjigo pred sončnim vzhodom. Stara tabela pravi devet metrov, brez lomljenja. Wenna pravi, da je ton A, lom nekje po osmi. Tvoja pravi, da predvalovanje doseže Run okoli šest štirideset in da Reža ostane mirna z nizkim G-jem. Pip ob prvem svitu odpelje čolnič in zapiše, kaj sliši. Če tvoja v nečem, kar lahko vidimo, ne premaga obeh drugih, je nihče ne uporabi.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ji dodaj številko, pri kateri me lahko ujameš. Zapiši širino loma. Če se ne more zmotiti na način, ki ga lahko vidiš, ni napoved, ampak prerokba, eno takšnih pa sem ti že dala.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Kako široko?

**Illuminara**  
Dvesto metrov beline čez Run. Zapiši to zadnje, pod druge, v mojem imenu.
Marit je zapisala. Njeno pero ni omahovalo in Illuminara je razumela, da se je pravkar naredila lažje zavrnljivo in da je prišla storit prav to.

**Marit Okonjo**  
In če imaš prav?

**Illuminara**  
Potem še vedno ni moje, da jo uporabim.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ne. Wenna po radiu kliče oznake. Jaz pokličem floto s svojim glasom, ker se bodo odzvali na mojega. Ti ostaneš na pomolu.

**Illuminara**  
Šestnajstletnica v čolniču pod valovanjem.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Je najboljša krmarka čolniča v ožini in jaz sem na radiu. Pravilo prekinitve: če Pip v Reži zasliši karkoli višjega od B-ja, je voda plitvejša od osmih metrov in flota ostane zunaj v zavetrju Ganneta z morskimi sidri. Reže nikoli ne razglasim za varno. To enainšestdeset čolnov stane noč na sidru v slabem vetru. Vem, koliko stane. Pravim ti, da je to moj strošek.

Illuminara ni takoj odgovorila. Do tega čolniča je lahko prišla na mnogo načinov, ne da bi čakala na pomolu, in dvorana ni zapisala nobenega pravila proti kateremukoli izmed njih. Vedela je tudi, da bi bila pot, ki jo flota uporabi zato, ker je ona odšla in jo naredila varno, njena, celotno nočno delo pa je bilo namenjeno temu, da nastane pot, ki ne bo.

**Illuminara**  
Strinjam se. Z vsem.

**Marit Okonjo**  
To ti je vzelo nekaj časa.

**Illuminara**  
Vzelo je toliko časa, kolikor ga je moralo.
Marit je obrnila stran v knjigi, ki je ni bilo treba prebrati.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Tobiah.

**Illuminara**  
Dve mesti. Z vrtinci pilotov v izračunu zanašanja se zoži na polico Gull Tooth, kamor po Wenninih besedah plima odloži vse, kar plava, ali na Tail Race. Tail Raca nihče ne preživi. Današnja spomladanska plima prekrije polico malo po drugi popoldne. Čoln mora biti tam do pol dvanajstih, skozi notranji prehod. Tisto ni Run. Zaščiteno je.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ne govori mi, da je živ.

**Illuminara**  
Ne vem, ali je. Na pomolu bom, dokler ne bo bodisi na njem bodisi ti nekdo ne pove, da ga ne bo.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Nisem te prosila, da ostaneš.

**Illuminara**  
Vem. Pravim ti, kje bom.

Marit ni rekla ničesar. Svetilka je sikala. Zunaj v temi je nekdo že vlekel čolnič po klančini navzdol. Pip, je spoznala Illuminara, ki je bila budna tako dolgo kot vse druge in je nihče ni prosil, naj spi.

scenes.title: Preizkus
paragraphs: *Little Skerry, pristaniški pomol · sedemnajst ur pred drugo nevihto, 06.30*

Radio je stal na prevrnjenem zaboju med Marit in Illuminari in nobena ga ni pogledala. Wennin glas je prihajal iz njega suh in raven, ko je klicala oznake, kakor da bere jedilnik. Zunaj na Runu se je majhna luč premikala proti sivemu morju. Predvalovanje je bilo že vidno kot počasno dvigovanje obzorja, kakor da se nekaj velikega obrača v spanju.

**Pip Marren**  
Oznaka Runa. Imam A. Čisti A je. Sipina je tam, kjer je rekla Wenna.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Valovanje?

**Pip Marren**  
Dolgo. Dolgo in nizko in dviguje me.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Šest osemintrideset.
Marit ni govorila nikomur. Tri liste papirja je stiskala v pesti.

**Pip Marren**  
Pod menoj se dviguje. Grem proti Reži. Wenna, zdaj grem proti Reži.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Pojdi.

Illuminara je slišala, kako so se vrtljaji motorja dvignili. Čolnič je bil miljo proč pod nebom, ki se je lomilo, v njem eno samo dekle, Illuminara pa bi lahko bila ob njem, še preden bi se končal naslednji stavek. Stala je na pomolu z rokami ob telesu, ker je rekla, da bo, in ker pot, skozi katero mora sama prenesti dekle, ni pot. To je bil najtežji račun noči, odgovor pa je bil, da ne naredi nič.

**Pip Marren**  
Tam gre. O. O, lomi se. Belo se lomi čez ves Run. Več kot dvesto je, ne vem, tristo petdeset, vidim ves rob.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Šest enainštirideset.
Marit ni pogledala Illuminare. Ni ji bilo treba. Sto petdeset metrov beline tam, kjer je ob njenem imenu na listu pisalo dvesto.

**Pip Marren**  
Pri ustju Reže sem. Dviguje se. B je. Ni mirno, Wenna, B je.

**Marit Okonjo**  
B ni višji od B-ja.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Ustje je. Reža se začne severneje, kot misli tvoje dekle. Pip, štirideset metrov. Ob belem stebru in nato štirideset. Poslušaj G.

**Illuminara**  
Moja je imela ustje preveč južno.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Tvoja ga je imela tam, kamor je zemljevid postavil stari greben. Tudi greben je hodil vstran. Jaz to slišim. Ti nisi mogla.

**Pip Marren**  
Severno štirideset. Severno, severno. Tam. G. To je G, Wenna, miren je, dviguje se, a nič se ne lomi.
Na pomolu ni nihče spregovoril. Marit je še enkrat prebrala tri liste, nato pa jih počasi, enkrat samkrat, brez hitenja odložila na zaboj.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Tabela je rekla brez loma. Napačno. Wenna je prav določila sipino, uro zgrešila za uro in pol, ustje pa imela prav. Tvoja je imela uro na minuto, Režo, širino zgrešeno za sto petdeset in ustje za štirideset. Wennino uho je premaknilo tvoje ustje, tvoja ura pa njen lom. Nobena sama ne spravi čolna skozi.

**Illuminara**  
Moja sipina je prišla od Wenne.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ura pa od tebe, iz poti, pri kateri si se zmotila, in obdobja valovanja, ki si ga pravilno določila. Uporabila bom drugo.
Vzela je mikrofon flote in za hip je bilo videti, kakor da roka ne pripada njej.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Gannet Roads, tukaj Marit Okonjo, kapitanka flote, Little Skerry. Vstopite skozi Režo, tristo severno od Runa in ne skozi Run, ter štirideset mimo belega stebra. Wenna Tolliver pri zunanji oznaki kliče ton. Prečkate pri G-ju ali nižje. Če slišite B, čakate, spustite morska sidra in jaz bom odgovarjala za to. To je moja odločitev. Ponovite mi jo.

Glasovi so se vračali drug za drugim, prasketajoče, enainšestdeset jih je bilo, vsak je iste štiri stavke ponovil z drugačnim naglasom. Illuminara jih je štela in ugotovila, da joče, ne da bi to opazila. Z dlanjo si je obrisala obraz, kakor da je na njem morski pršec.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Tvoje ime je v knjigi.

**Illuminara**  
Kje?

**Marit Okonjo**  
Na levi. V stolpcu, ki ga Wenna vodi za to, pri čemer smo se zmotili. Sama ga je zapisala, še preden si sedla.

scenes.title: Gull Tooth
paragraphs: *Polica Gull Tooth, zunanji otočki · trinajst ur pred drugo nevihto, 11.10*

Šli so skozi notranji prehod, ki je bil zaščiten in počasen, v čolnu, ki ga je krmarila Marit sama. Rekla je, da bo Illuminara šla zraven, držala svetilko in se ne bo dotaknila nobene vrvi. Pip, premočena in žareča, je sedela na krmi s hidrofonom v naročju. Wennin glas iz dvorane je v zvočniku brnel kakor žuželka v kozarcu.

Gull Tooth je bila črna polica v velikosti kuhinje, ki jo je zalil vsak tretji val, pred njo pa greben, kjer se je valovanje dvignilo in padlo. Na njej sta bili dve postavi, privezani na stebriček, ukrivljen od neke razbitine, in tretja oblika, dolga in negibna, zavita v rumeno pelerino.

**Pip Marren**  
Marit. Dva od njih stojita.
Marit ni odgovorila. Eno roko je imela na ročici za plin, členki pa so postali barve kosti.

**Illuminara**  
Sunek na grebenu je deset minut visok, nato popušča. Naslednje zatišje traja enajst minut in se začne čez devetdeset sekund. Če je vrzel tam, kamor jo postavljajo zapiski pilotov, imate čas za en prehod.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Vrzel je dve dolžini čolna južno od belega stebra, pri E-ju. Če slišiš E, greš. Če slišiš F, se ustaviš in jaz te bom preklinjala.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Pip.

**Pip Marren**  
E. Imam E.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Potem gremo.

Trajalo je štiri minute, čoln se je spuščal in dvigal, hidrofon je pel svoj edini ton, Maritino mokro lice pa je bilo obrnjeno proti polici. Val se je dvignil za njimi, omahoval in šel mimo. Nato so bili pod stebričkom in svetilka je osvetlila dva siva, zabuhla obraza; eden se je smejal na nemočen način človeka, ki tega ni pričakoval.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Vzelo ti je nekaj časa.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Bila sem v dvorani.

Vse tri ljudi so dvignili čez ograjo, najprej Lise Harrow, nato Tobiaha in potem dolgo rumeno obliko. Dov Hallam je bil mrtev, in sicer že od prve noči, je povedal Tobiah, zato ga je privezal tja. Samo Marit se ga je dotaknila, nežno, tako kot se je nekoč dotikala svojih spečih otrok. Ines Varga ni bila na polici. Tobiah je to enkrat tiho povedal pri krmilu, Marit pa je pokimala in ga ni prisilila, da bi to ponovil.
Na poti nazaj je čez čoln pogledal neznanko, ki je držala svetilko.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Marit pravi, da si na pomolu izgovorila naša imena. Preden je kdo vprašal.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem vedela, kdo od vas je živ.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Pravi, da si rekla prav to.
Illuminara je držala svetilko, dokler je ni začela boleti roka. Ni je odložila, ker ji nihče ni rekel, da sme.

scenes.title: Štetje
paragraphs: *Little Skerry, valobran in Dvorana pilotov · dve uri in pol pred drugo nevihto, 21.30*

Dež je prišel zgodaj. Dvainpetdeset trupov je bilo že noter in svetilka na valobranu jih je pokazala enega za drugim, ko so drseli mimo pomola, vsak kapitan je stal pri krmilu in ni gledal nikogar. Wenna je štela s škrbino svinčnika in jezikom med zobmi. Marit je stala na koncu valobrana z mikrofonom flote v pesti. Illuminara je stala dva koraka za njo, kjer so ji rekli, s svetilko, ki ji je visela iz roke. Zunaj pri ustju Reže je Pipin čolnič jezdil na valovanju s spuščenim hidrofonom, zvočnik na valobranu pa je prenašal, kar je slišala Pip: dolg, enakomeren G, kakor zadržan dih.

**Pip Marren**  
Dvainpetdeset noter. G. Naslednji je Rook.

**Aud Hallam**  
Marit, Rook. Oznako imam na očeh. Prihajam skozi.
Maritin palec je bil že na tipki, ko se je ton premaknil.

**Pip Marren**  
B. Imam B.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
B je dovoljen.

**Pip Marren**  
B je in hodi. Marit, C je.
Pravilo je bilo zapisano v knjigo ob štirih zjutraj in od takrat ni bilo nič drugega kot črnilo.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Držite. Vsi čolni, držite. Rook, drži. Morska sidra dol in glave pokonci.

**Aud Hallam**  
Marit. Šestnajst ur sem na tej vodi, da pridem k sinu. Leži na klopi v tvoji dvorani, jaz pa zamujam šestnajst ur. Ne prisili me čakati zaradi tona.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Počakala boš.

**Aud Hallam**  
Čigava številka je to?

**Marit Okonjo**  
Moja.
Marit je spustila mikrofon in, ne da bi obrnila glavo, spregovorila osebi za seboj.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Je Reža ali sunek?

**Illuminara**  
Sunek. Pulz na grebenu traja deset minut in zadnja dva sta trajala deset. Ton bi moral pasti čez približno šest.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Bi moral.

**Illuminara**  
Bi moral. Čakala bi, dokler Pip ne reče G, ne glede na vse.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Nisem te spraševala, kdaj. Spraševala sem, kaj.

**Illuminara**  
Vem.
Trajalo je sedem minut. Na valobranu ni nihče spregovoril, veter pa se je ujel v radio in zapel ton po svoje.

**Pip Marren**  
G. G, Marit. Spustil se je. G.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Najprej Rook. Pridi skozi.
Prišli so skozi, devet trupov v dežju, zadnja svetilka pa je pokazala kapitanko Rooka pri krmilu z dvignjeno brado. Ko je šla mimo pomola, je njen glas prišel iz zvočnika, miren in ne namenjen morju.

**Aud Hallam**  
Je tam? Ženska, ki je računala.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Za menoj je.

**Aud Hallam**  
Prvi račun me je stal mojega fanta. Drugi me je pripeljal k njemu. Nosila bom oba in ne boš me prosila, naj katerega odložim.

**Illuminara**  
Ne.
Enainšestdeseti trup je zdrsnil mimo pomola ob dvaindvajset petintrideset. Wenna je naredila kljukico v knjigi iz jadrovine in sedla na najbližji privezni stebriček, kakor da so ji vzeli noge.

V notranjosti je bila svetilka zastrta. Tobiah je ležal na klopi pod odejo s skodelico juhe. Lise so odpeljali domov. Dov je ležal pod sivo odejo na koncu dvorane, njegova mati pa je sedela ob njem z roko na odeji in hrbtom proti prostoru.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Ne odpuščam ti.

**Illuminara**  
Ne.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Hči Ines Varga pristane v četrtek. Povedala ji boš, kar si povedala meni, v tej dvorani, z odprto knjigo, ona pa bo rekla, kar bo hotela. Če ne reče nič, je nič. Če bo huje od tega, kar sem rekla jaz, boš poslušala.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Ko morje upade, greva s Pip s čolničem do vrtinca Tail Race. Ena oznaka na uro med oseko, petnajst jih bo. Ti nama daš valovanje za vsako oznako, midve pa poveva, katera oznaka. Če se hči želi peljati zraven, se pelje.

**Illuminara**  
Prinesla bom valovanje. Vi izberete oznako.

**Marit Okonjo**  
In ko bo naslednjič nevihta, vprašaš dvorano, preden poveš pristanišču. Ne potem. Prej. V knjigi, kot pravilo.

**Illuminara**  
Sama ga bom zapisala. S svojo roko, na levo.
Marit se je skoraj nasmehnila, pa je nasmeh ugasnil kot vžigalica na prepihu.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Lise pravi, da ženska s svetilko je ni nikoli odložila, Marit.

**Marit Okonjo**  
Nihče ji ni rekel, da sme.

**Tobiah Okonjo**  
Potem bi ji nekdo moral.
Nihče ji ni. Illuminara je ugotovila, da je nehala čakati na to.

Wenna je prišla z mraza in stala ob peči, z nje je kapljalo. Knjigo iz jadrovine je položila odprto na mizo, zdaj s tremi stolpci tam, kjer sta bila prej dva: kaj je rekla tabela, kaj je rekla voda, kaj je dvorana storila glede tega. Pod prvo nevihto je levi stolpec vseboval vrstico v njeni stari oglati pisavi. Illuminara jo je prebrala in ni odvrnila pogleda.

**Wenna Tolliver**  
Pridi sem in poslušaj to.

Vključila je zvočnik na koncu mize. Zunaj onkraj valobrana je hidrofon še vedno visel tam, kjer ga je pustila Pip, skozi dež pa je prenašal dolg, nizek, enakomeren ton, G, zvok poti, odprte v temi, z enainšestdesetimi trupi, ki so počivali nad njo, in sto dvajsetimi miljami vremena, ki je prihajalo za njimi in ni našlo ničesar, kar bi lahko zlomilo.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara prizna usodne omejitve svoje prve napovedi, se uči iz Wenninega poslušanja plime, naredi svojo novo napoved zavrnljivo in zmotljivo ter pomaga Marit pripeljati domov enainšestdeset čolnov, ne da bi ljudem pristanišča odvzela njihovo znanje ali pristojnost.
